## Summary

Huawei Device Co., Ltd. is Huawei's consumer-device company: Huawei's consumer privacy statement is issued by "Huawei Device Co., Ltd. and its global affiliates" and covers feature phones, smartphones, laptops, tablets, wearables, mobile broadband devices and smart home appliances [2]. The IEEE registry lists 640 MA-L blocks to it at Xincheng Road, Songshan Lake, Dongguan, separate from the blocks of "HUAWEI TECHNOLOGIES CO.,LTD", which has its own entry [1]. Huawei itself was founded in Shenzhen in 1987, sold its Honor brand to a Shenzhen state-owned enterprise in 2020 under US sanctions, and ships HarmonyOS, which succeeded EMUI, on its phones, tablets, watches and PCs [6].

A MAC in a Huawei Device block is therefore most likely a Huawei phone, tablet, laptop, watch or home device [2], though no source consulted ties a specific model to a specific block. As an example of the radios, the HUAWEI Mate X6 lists 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax 2x2 on 2.4 and 5 GHz, Bluetooth 5.2 with BLE and 4G LTE, running EMUI 15 [3]. iFixit's Mate 20 Pro teardown found HiSilicon's own Hi1103 Wi-Fi chipset beside the Kirin 980 [4].

Huawei publishes monthly security bulletins for its phones and tablets; the August 2026 bulletin lists 33 CVEs including a Wi-Fi enhancement module flaw, CVE-2026-49305 [5]. In November 2022 the US FCC banned sales and imports of Huawei equipment [6]. The founding year of this legal entity, FCC grantee codes and randomization behaviour are not documented here: the FCC ID databases refused requests from the session that wrote this entry.
